svg.title: It is not the recursion. It is the repetition.
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing the full fib(5) recursion tree with every occurrence of fib(2) ringed in red and fib(3) in amber, annotated with 29,860,703 naive calls for fib(35); the same tree with the repeated subtrees struck out and a memo table being filled, annotated with 69 calls and a 432,764 times reduction; an edit-distance grid between kitten and sitting with one cell highlighted and three arrows entering it from above, from the left and from the diagonal labelled delete, insert and substitute; and a memory comparison of a 634.67 megabyte full matrix struck through against 0.33 megabytes for two rows, with the warning that two rows cannot reconstruct the alignment path.
svg.text: It is not the recursion. It is the repetition.
it is not the recursion that is slow. It is
the REPETITION. The tree is mostly the same
few answers, computed again and again.
and you only ever look at the previous row
but two rows gives you the NUMBER and cannot give you
the PATH. Keeping the whole matrix is what buys you the
